title: Manus researches and codes a live website for a personal design-history collection
summary: A collector asked Manus to build a website showcasing items such as a signed Frank Lloyd Wright autobiography, with researched artifact details and downloadable citations, and could replay the agent's steps.
agent_role: Manus researched each artifact, wrote the site code and deployed it over hours; the author supplied the collection and requested fixes iteratively, sometimes days later.
outcome: Author says Manus turned the basement-collection hobby into a fully functional website with rich research and custom code
what_they_did: The InnovationTraining.org author asked Manus for a live website showcasing their design-history collection, with research, artifact details and downloadable citations. In one chat they uploaded four artifact images, shared links to blog posts and eBay listings, and flagged items that needed provenance research. Over one to two hours Manus identified the items, checked details on museum, academic and niche Facebook sources, wrote the site code and filled in the pages.
how_it_went: The author says Manus delivered a polished site with custom branding in Wright's "Taliesin red," downloadable research PDFs and a checked-off to-do list. They say it turned a basement-collection hobby into a fully functional website, and that the replay view let them audit every step.
worth_knowing: The author warns that an agent may take hours, unlike a chatbot. They say it works best with both images and links to cross-reference. The post also includes the author's Manus invite link.
prompt: Build a live website that showcases my collection of [type of items]. I am uploading photos of [number] items and sharing these links: [blog posts, listings or other sources]. For each item, identify the title, creator and era. Check those details against museum archives, academic sites and other reputable sources, and mark anything you could not confirm. Give each item a page with a description, its historical significance and a "Further Reading" list of citations, plus a downloadable research PDF. Use a clean, responsive design with [preferred colors or style]. Keep a to-do list as you work. Show me the draft site and your sources, and wait for my approval before publishing it.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
